title: GLOBE: Accurate Surrogates for Boundary-Driven PDEs via Domain-Inspired Architectures and Equivariance
claim: A complex model decomposes hierarchically into stacked, zoomed-in stages, with built-in symmetry mechanisms making the whole architecture principled.
layout: 3 stacked panels, top-to-bottom zoom, left-to-right flow, dashed equivariance callout
description: Three stacked horizontal bands show an architecture at progressively finer zoom, joined by gray zoom lines and captions. The top band is a left-to-right chain of boxes: Inputs (peach), Initialize, Hyperlayers 0, 1, ..., H (green), Calibration and Output (purple). The middle band, in a rounded container, shows Inputs fanning out to n parallel kernel boxes with different effective length scales (teal). These merge into a summation node and then an Output box. The bottom band is a linear chain of boxes: Input Assembly, Invariant Features, Padé MLP, Far-Field Decay (with a formula), Vector Reprojection, Aggregation, Output. A dashed callout in the lower right lists the equivariance mechanisms. Peach marks inputs, blue/teal marks computation, and purple marks outputs. The eye starts at the top-left Inputs box.
caption: GLOBE architecture. The model operates at three hierarchical levels. Top: Communication hyperlayers propagate latent information between boundary partitions before ﬁnal evaluation. Middle: Each hyperlayer contains multiscale kernels operating at different reference length scales, with outputs summed. Bottom: Individual kernels evaluate all-to-all source-to-target inﬂuences through invariant feature engineering, Padé-approximant networks, far-ﬁeld decay envelopes, and equivariant vector reprojection, then aggregate over sources weighted by strengths and face areas.
abstract: We introduce GLOBE, a nonlinear neural surrogate for boundary-driven, homogeneous, weakly nonlinear PDEs that draws inductive bias from boundary-element methods and equivariant ML, representing solutions as superpositions of learnable Green's-function-like kernels evaluated from boundary faces to targets. The architecture is translation-, rotation-, and parity-equivariant; discretization-invariant; and units-invariant via rigorous nondimensionalization. On AirFRANS (steady incompressible RANS over NACA airfoils), a compact ~117k-parameter GLOBE model has lower mean-squared error than published values for the strongest reported ML surrogates on both the interpolation and low-data splits, in single-run comparisons under the released AirFRANS normalization. The model evaluates fields at arbitrary points, handles non-watertight meshes, and generalizes under Reynolds number and angle-of-attack distribution shifts. We further introduce a hierarchical Barnes-Hut acceleration that exploits the kernel's far-field decay to reduce evaluation cost from quadratic to near-linear in the number of boundary elements, with a tunable opening angle that recovers exact dense evaluation in the zero-angle limit. Quantitative validation focuses on 2D AirFRANS; on 3D DrivAerML cars, GLOBE predicts surface and volume fields on the full meshes, and we compare it with a matched Transolver baseline. Together, these results show that boundary-element-inspired inductive biases can substantially improve the accuracy of ML surrogates for boundary-driven PDEs while scaling to large 3D meshes.
